design.title: Rotation-consensus decode: confidence = agreement across four headings, baked into the exported graph
design.eli5: The model sometimes lands confidently on the wrong farm field because, from one angle, it looks identical to the right one. So before trusting an answer, we now show the model the same photo four times, turned 90 degrees each time -- like double-checking a guess by looking at the map from four directions. A place it truly knows gets the same answer every time; a lucky look-alike match changes its answer when the picture turns. When the four answers disagree, the model now says 'I don't know' instead of feeding a wrong position to the aircraft -- and for this aircraft, a wrong answer is far more dangerous than no answer.
design.hypothesis: Prignitz's entire gap to Berlin is false fixes (3.75% vs 0.50%; usable, abstention and median error barely move). The mechanism CLAUDE.md diagnoses is belief mass landing confidently on ONE wrong field that looks like the right one -- a case single-view pooled-mass confidence cannot see, because a wrong unimodal peak is indistinguishable from a right one. But training draws a fresh uniform-random heading per position per epoch, so a genuinely memorized place is heading-invariant by construction, while a false match to a look-alike twin rides view-specific micro-texture cues that should not survive rotating the same frame. Requiring cross-heading consensus therefore separates the two cases: right answers keep their pooled mass, heading-dependent wrong answers split their mass across distant blocks and drop below the frozen 0.3 confidence threshold, converting false fixes into abstentions at zero training cost. If instead usable_fix_rate collapses, we learn the aliasing is rotation-stable -- equally decisive, and it would redirect the era toward training-time disambiguation.
